newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania airline Tarom gets new management.
newsitem.headline: Romania airline Tarom gets new management.

text.p: Romania's state-owned airline Tarom got a new general manager on Friday in a move intended to pave the way to company restructuring, the country's main privatisation agency said.

The move to replace the carrier's manager is aimed at ensuring the success of the restructuring programme and at making the company profitable, said a statement by the State Ownership Fund (FPS), Tarom's majority shareholder.
The statement offered no more details and FPS officials were unavailable for immediate comment.
The FPS had previously announced plans to rapidly restructure the airline including layoffs and the sale of its outdated Soviet-made aircraft.

Romania's national carrier Tarom has laboured under huge debts in recent years, compounded by high fees to air traffic control and airport authorities. Local media reports put the airline's internal debt at the equivalent of some $11.1 million and external debts at $15.5 million.

A restructuring plan to make Tarom competitive in east European markets was initiated in 1995 but stalled under leftists who held power after the collapse of Communism in 1989 until their election defeat last year.
